scope: Current published commercial line inventory, not a complete daily timetable and not a reconstruction of 1 January 2022. 15 corporate nuclei, 63 commuter line/branch codes, 6 Catalan regional codes and one associated tram-train. Every commuter endpoint matched to an official Renfe station record.
license: Factual compilation with source URLs. Underlying station catalogues: CC BY 4.0; do not infer PDF artwork license.

stationCatalogueNotes: 1009 unique stations in current Renfe complete catalogue; supplement with 13 legacy tables for missing Cercanías and FEVE stops. Combined deduplicated station set has 1494 records.
Renfe station numeric codes are not GTFS stop_id; reconcile imported stops by ID mapping/name and geographic evidence.
Intermediate waypoints select logical route branch and must not be presented as full stopping pattern.
Route geometry remains null because source diagrams are schematic. Use imported GTFS shapes or verified OSM railway topology with gauge matching.
Service train numbers, rolling stock series and physical unit identities are absent from the station catalogue; never invent them.
Some legacy coordinates are wrong in the original data. Prefer current 2026 catalogue on the same numeric ID and preserve source age.
temporalNotes: Bilbao C5 commenced on 2026-05-06: exclude from starting 2022 network unless a future unlock.
Current Rodalies RL3/RL4 and station names must not be backdated to 2022 without historical records.
Asturias map January 2026: C5a Gijón–Oviedo via El Berrón; C7 San Esteban–Oviedo. Older OSP contracts used a wider C7 denomination.
Infrastructure interruptions and alternative bus arrangements vary daily; the commercial map is not the operating timetable.
